subject.title: Control UI: Pinned context panel for user-defined persistent facts

question: Should pinned user facts be a first-class core Control UI memory surface, and what storage plus injection contract should OpenClaw own?
rationale: The remaining work is not just UI plumbing: it decides prompt-influencing persistent state, stale-fact semantics, browser write boundaries, and whether core, the memory panel, or plugin contribution slots own the experience.

options.title: Design First-Class Pinned Facts
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify a narrow core pinned-facts model with always-injected versus last-seen semantics, diff-preview saves, and explicit security boundaries before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Memory Panel
options.body: Treat pinned facts as a subfeature of the broader memory editor tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46809, so memory files and pinned facts share one UX and security review.

options.title: Defer To Plugin Panel Seam
options.body: Wait for the broader Control UI contribution-slot direction at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71736 and let a memory/plugin owner provide the panel through that API.

recommendation.title: Design First-Class Pinned Facts
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify a narrow core pinned-facts model with always-injected versus last-seen semantics, diff-preview saves, and explicit security boundaries before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history signal for the adjacent Gateway workspace boundary and file-access contract that this product/security decision would cross.
